claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me at home. I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know about Alex.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

**Are you responsible for Alex's care and do you pay for his day-to-day needs such as food, clothes, and other expenses?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. Alex lives with me and I'm responsible for all his day-to-day needs - his food, clothes, school things, everything really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or living with someone else for any extended period of time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, I should mention that I'm fostering Alex. But no, he's not in hospital or in care - he lives here with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that important detail about fostering Alex.

**Is the local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance costs while you're fostering him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about that, to be honest. I don't know if the council is paying anything or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about that. This is actually an important detail for determining your eligibility for Child Benefit when fostering a child.

According to the rules, you can get Child Benefit for a foster child **as long as the local council is not paying anything towards their accommodation or maintenance**. Since you're unsure whether the council is making any payments, I cannot make a definite determination about your eligibility.

**I'd recommend that you:**
- Check with your local council or your fostering agency to find out if they are paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance
- Once you have that information, you can make a more informed decision about whether to claim
- You can also contact the Child Benefit Office directly who can help clarify your specific situation

Based on the information provided, I need to report that your eligibility is indeterminate due to this missing crucial information.

conversation.text: I hope this helps clarify your situation. If you find out the information about council payments and would like to discuss your eligibility further, please feel free to come back. Good luck!
